title: PR #6490 moved structure-board rendering into a new generic render_object_structure admin endpoint and dropped the user_can_change_page check the old details() path applied, so any staff user can read the plugin structure of pages they may not view.

findings.explanation: The diff does not introduce any raw SQL queries or string interpolation into SQL. All data access appears to go through Django ORM methods.

Three new URL endpoints are registered — render_object_edit, render_object_structure, and render_object_preview — taking a content_type_id and object_id from the URL. These endpoints are registered under PlaceholderAdmin's url_patterns, but Django admin url_patterns are not automatically protected by the admin authentication/authorization wrappers (admin.site.admin_view) unless explicitly wrapped. If render_object_edit/structure/preview do not independently verify that the requesting user is authenticated and has the necessary permissions to access or edit the referenced object, this would constitute missing authorization (CWE-862) and potentially IDOR (CWE-639). The diff does not show the implementation of these view functions, so it is not possible to confirm whether they perform proper permission checks.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap each view with self.admin_site.admin_view() to ensure authentication and basic staff checks are enforced at the admin URL level, e.g. pat(r'^object/([0-9]+)/edit/([0-9]+)/$', self.admin_site.admin_view(render_object_edit)). Additionally, verify that each view function checks that the requesting user has the appropriate permissions for the specific object being accessed.
